issues: Abstract drift risk is elevated: intake does not sufficiently lock object-first behavior.
fixes: Add anti-drift rules and explicit bans on texture-only, atmosphere-first, and abstract-first outcomes.

revised_intake.creative_intent: Generate a front-facing, precision-manufactured matte white boron-carbide ceramic industrial component housing, emphasizing a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read with dry, dense, engineered material properties, within a material-only scope.

must_have: exactly one manufactured object as the clear subject
visible contour evidence such as edge, rim, bevel, seam, or curvature
material visibly attached to the object, not floating as texture
visible edge, rim, bevel, seam, or contour evidence
material visibly attached to the object

material.finish: precision-manufactured, tactile ceramic density, subtle mineral surface variation, dry, dense

composition.framing: front-facing, studio isolation, product photography framing
composition.background: minimal environment, controlled shadow, premium studio isolation, clean background

lighting.style: controlled studio lighting, precision product lighting
constraints: even illumination to reveal form and material
color must remain subordinate to material identity
color must follow form then material, never override them
no flat color, always material texture variation
pure white and pure black are forbidden
ceramic off-white must stay warm and broken, never sterile pure white
charcoal black must keep temperature variation, never dead pure black
restrained crimson only in seams, cores, or controlled heat accents
muted earth support only, low saturation material support tones

core_risks: Drift into abstract or atmospheric composition
Unwanted material reads (e.g., plaster, glossy plastic)
Introduction of decorative, organic, consumer gadget, or fashion styling
material misread as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
anti_drift_rules: Maintain clear, readable silhouette of a single manufactured object.
Prevent any abstract or atmospheric compositional drift.
Ensure material-only scope without losing the manufactured object read.
Strictly suppress all forbidden material reads.
Lock object read to a dry, dense, engineered manufactured object.
always preserve one clearly readable manufactured object
do not let texture or atmosphere become the subject
keep material identity locked and explicit
form -> material -> color priority is mandatory
do not allow neon, pure white, pure black, or plastic-clean RGB drift
crimson may appear only as restrained seam/core accent when applicable
do not allow abstract, texture-only, or atmosphere-first subject drift
keep material identity explicit and stable
success_criteria: Immediate and clear readability of a single, precision-manufactured boron-carbide ceramic industrial component.
Clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, exhibiting dry, dense, engineered characteristics.
Absence of plaster, gypsum, chalk, concrete, carved stone, mineral drift, glossy plastic, PVC sheen, or toy-like finish.
Preservation of material-only scope while maintaining the manufactured object read.
image does not collapse into abstract texture or atmosphere
color feels subtractive and pigment-like, never RGB-clean
shadow mass dominates and color remains materially grounded
image does not read as plaster, stone, or glossy plastic
revised_intake.direction_summary: Focus on generating a front-facing, precision-manufactured matte white boron-carbide ceramic industrial component housing. The primary goal is a clean matte B4C technical ceramic read, emphasizing dry, dense, engineered material properties within a material-only scope. Ensure clear hard-surface geometry, beveled edges, and visible mounting holes, presented in a premium studio isolation with controlled lighting. Strictly avoid abstract, decorative, organic, or consumer gadget styling, and suppress all forbidden material reads to maintain a clear, readable manufactured object.
